title: How Netanyahu Lost His Bet on Trump
gist: Azriel Bermant argues Netanyahu's all-in bet on Trump and the Republicans has backfired: Trump announced an end to U.S. military aid to Israel by year-end on midterm Election Day, the Iran war is blamed for the GOP midterm defeat, and Netanyahu, now a caretaker, retains incentives to gamble on renewed escalation with Iran.

themes.theme: End of U.S. military aid to Israel

insights.claim: Trump announced on Fox News on U.S. midterm Election Day that U.S. military assistance to Israel would end by year-end, claiming Netanyahu had agreed months ago.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Loss of U.S. aid pressures Israeli defense budget and procurement from U.S. contractors.
insights.quote: Bibi Netanyahu and I … made a deal months ago that we’re stopping, and they’re fine with it.
insights.locator: While Israelis were still coming to terms

insights.claim: Netanyahu had only said in January he hoped to taper aid dependence over the next decade, with no sign of agreeing to end it this year; his office now spins it as a transition to partnership and mutual investment.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Watch for replacement co-investment/partnership deals in defense.
insights.quote: transition out from aid towards partnership and mutual investment
insights.locator: It is true that Netanyahu told the Economist

insights.claim: Critics including Ehud Barak suspect the aid termination was a quid pro quo for Trump's endorsement of Netanyahu in Israel's Oct. 27 election.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Signals politicization of the U.S.-Israel security relationship.
insights.locator: Former Prime Minister Ehud Barak accused

insights.claim: Trump timed the announcement to resonate with voters angry about inflation and cost of living, reflecting collapse of Israel's standing across the U.S. political spectrum; the question of why a high-tech powerhouse needs taxpayer aid carries growing weight.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Foreign aid is becoming a domestic cost-of-living political issue.
insights.quote: why a high-tech powerhouse requires billions in taxpayer-funded military aid carries growing political weight
insights.locator: That Trump chose to make this announcement

themes.theme: Iran war blamed for GOP midterm loss

insights.claim: Vice President J.D. Vance publicly blamed the Iran war for the Republican midterm defeat, citing internal polling that 2024 Trump voters who defected wanted an end to the war, relief from soaring fuel prices and a change in the Israel relationship.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Political pressure for de-escalation and fuel-price relief is now intra-GOP.
insights.quote: The reason we lost is the war.
insights.locator: The real elephant in the room

insights.claim: Trump, on 60 Minutes, did not dispute that the Iran war caused the midterm defeat and said there is a great dislike for Israel.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Lame-duck Trump may pivot away from Israel-aligned escalation.
insights.quote: there is a great dislike, incredibly, for Israel
insights.locator: The real elephant in the room

insights.claim: By putting all his eggs in the Republican basket, Netanyahu has wrecked bipartisan U.S. support for Israel and now faces critics on the left and a Republican base seeking a scapegoat.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Structural erosion of U.S. political support raises Israel's long-run risk premium.
insights.quote: Netanyahu has wrecked U.S. bipartisan support for Israel

themes.theme: Netanyahu's incentive to escalate with Iran

insights.claim: Netanyahu has repeatedly pushed Trump to renew the Iran war, using the Iranian threat partly to distract voters from his Oct. 7 failures; U.S. officials were skeptical of Israeli intelligence on Iranian chemical-weapon plans, seeing it as a push for renewed strikes.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Treat Israeli escalation signals with skepticism but as a live risk.
insights.locator: While it was Trump who launched a war

insights.claim: Netanyahu's stated endgame of toppling Iran's regime conflicts with the Trump administration's aim of using force as leverage to reopen Hormuz and force a nuclear climbdown.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: U.S.-Israel divergence on war aims makes a U.S.-led settlement more likely than regime change.
insights.locator: Netanyahu’s endgame is clearly at odds

insights.claim: Netanyahu's push for confrontation caused an unprecedented rift with IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir, who resisted orders risking an unwarranted regional conflagration.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Military pushback constrains unilateral Israeli escalation.
insights.locator: Netanyahu’s rhetoric on Iran is riddled

insights.claim: Trump says renewed war is highly unlikely if Iran talks progress, but ally Chris Ruddy put an 80% chance on Trump still authorizing military action against Tehran.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Market should keep substantial probability on renewed U.S. strikes on Iran.
insights.quote: there was an 80 percent chance that the U.S. president could still authorize military action against Tehran

insights.claim: Netanyahu remains caretaker PM while opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, holding the mandate, tries to form a government; Arab parties are pivotal kingmakers, making coalition-building highly uncertain.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Israeli political instability may persist; watch coalition outcome.

insights.claim: Shin Bet chief David Zini, a Netanyahu loyalist, has targeted Arab opposition lawmakers with unfounded investigations, raising constitutional alarm.
insights.speaker: Azriel Bermant
insights.so_what: Institutional erosion risk for Israel's democratic standing and sovereign perception.
